title: Simulate a population using the dynamic pool model
text: simyears minLL require single numeric value. example simulates population 50 years minimum length limit 400mm. lhparms requires list vector created makeLH() function. makeLH() function creates list life history parameters needed. Including, initial number recruits, maximum age fish population, von Bertalanffy growth model parameters (L∞L_\infty, KK, t0t_0), parameters log10-transformed weight length model (alpha beta). default, makeLH() returns list. Growth length-weight model paramaters can generated functions FSA package. See Make Life History object article details. example uses following life history parameters: cf cm matrix rows = simyears (number years specified simulation) columns = tmax (maximum age). example assigns cm 0 first year 0.18 remaining years constant across ages; cf 0 first year 0.33 remaining years constant across ages. Note, Ages must age-0 maximum age. Thus, cf cm matrix maximum age plus one rows. Recruitment must vector length simyears contain single value year. Users can specify vector manually use genRecruits() function allows user specify different trends recruitment. example sets recruitment fixed 1000 individuals year.

text: Simulates dynamics exploited fish populations using Jones modification Beverton-Holt equilibrium yield equation compute yield-per-recruit dynamic pool models (Ricker 1975) https://publications.gc.ca/site/eng/480738/publication.html. Allows users evaluate minimum, slot, inverted length limits exploited fisheries using specified life history parameters. Users can simulate population variety conditional fishing mortality conditional natural mortality. Calculated quantities include number fish harvested dying naturally, mean weight length fish harvested, number fish reach specified lengths interest, total number fish biomass population, stock density indices. package maintained Jason Doll, Associate Professor Fisheries Francis Marion University

code: # Load other required packages for organizing output and plotting library(dplyr)    ## for filter library(ggplot2)  ## for ggplot et al. library(metR)     ## geom_contour2  # Life history parameters to be used below LH <- makeLH(N0=100,tmax=15,Linf=592,K=0.20,t0=-0.3,LWalpha=-5.528,LWbeta=3.273)  # Estimate yield for multiple values of minLL, cf, and cm # # This is a minimal example, increments for minLL, cf, and cm would likely be smaller # #   to produce finer-scaled results.  minLL <- seq(from = 200, to = 550, by = 50) cf <- seq(from = 0.1, to = 0.9, by = 0.1) cm <- seq(from = 0.1, to = 0.9, by = 0.1) loi <- c(400,450,500,550)  Res_1 <- yprBH_MinLL(minLL = minLL, cf = cf, cm = cm,                      lhparms=LH, loi=loi)  # Yield curves (yield vs exploitation) by varying minimum lengths, # using cm=40 plot_dat <- Res_1 |> filter(cm==0.40)  ggplot(data=plot_dat,mapping=aes(y=yield,x=exploitation,                                  group=minLL,color=minLL)) +   geom_line(linewidth=1) +   scale_color_gradient2(high="black") +   xlab("Exploitation (u)")+   ylab("Yield (g)")+   labs(color="Min Length Limit") +   theme_bw()   # Yield isopleths for varying minLL and exploitation with cm=0.40 # # Using same data as previous example ggplot(data=plot_dat,mapping=aes(x=exploitation,y=minLL,z=yield)) +   geom_contour2(aes(label = after_stat(level))) +   xlab("Exploitation (u)") +   ylab("Minimum length limit (mm)") +   theme_bw()
